record.text: JMIR Res Protocols: Uncovering the Experiences of Basti-Dwelling Adolescent Girls Who Menstruate in Hyderabad, India: #Protocol for a Multimethod Critical Qualitative #Study

external.description: Background: Rapid urbanization in India is straining the government’s capacity to provide basic amenities such as housing, sanitation, electricity, and water. One group of people who are deeply affected are adolescent girls who menstruate. In urban slums, referred to as bastis in Telugu and Hindi, this reality is worsened by spatial congestion and limited water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) resources. This #Study is situated in the populous slum colonies of Film Nagar, Hyderabad, where residents navigate precarious living conditions and a scarcity of basic amenities. Objective: In this context, we argue that menstrual experiences are profoundly shaped by an interplay of biological, sociopolitical, and environmental factors. This #Study aims to examine how these intersecting dimensions shape the menstrual experiences of slum-dwelling adolescent girls (aged 8‐18 years) in Film Nagar by understanding the (1) sociocultural and political discourse, (2) intergenerational household power dynamics, and (3) the enabling environment. Methods: Guided by biopolitics and poststructuralist feminist theory, we use a critical ethnographic approach involving intergenerational households (adolescent girls, mothers, fathers, and unmarried brothers aged 15‐24 years). Approximately 18‐28 informants across 5‐8 households will be recruited using maximum variation, purposive, and snowball sampling, targeting. Data generation includes rapport-building, participant observation (journaling, voice recordings, photography, or transect walks), document analysis, focus group discussions (FGDs), and in-depth interviews (IDIs). Analysis occurs concurrently using frame analysis: transcripts undergo value or narrative coding to inductively identify codes, followed by axial and selective coding to group codes into discourses interpreted through our theoretical framework, yielding dominant frames addressing each #Research question. Findings will inform a #Digital storytelling output along with a 3-paper thesis and peer-reviewed journal publication. Results: This #Study is part of the primary author’s doctoral dissertation, funded by the Social Sciences and Humanities #Research Council (SSHRC) Doctoral Fellowship (2023‐2026) and the International Development #Research Centre (IDRC) International Doctoral #Research Award (2024‐2025). Ethics approval was obtained from the University of Toronto and University of Hyderabad #Research ethics boards in January 2025. Recruitment closed in September 2025 with 18 households enrolled. Data collection closed in March 2026. #Protocol deviations included narrowing the #Study from 5 to 2 slum colonies due to time constraints, resequencing methods to begin with maternal focus groups to build trust, shifting to small group discussions in participants’ homes, adding ethnographic interviews, and permitting verbal consent; 3 of these changes required #Research Ethics Board (REB) amendment. Dissemination is anticipated by September 2027. Conclusions: This #Study is expected to (1) clarify how sociopolitical, familial, and environmental factors interact to shape menstrual experiences among adolescent girls in urban slums and (2) inform context-sensitive menstrual health policies and programs for similar low-resource settings. International Registered Report Identifier (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/94012

record.text: JMIR Res Protocols: Vitamin D Supplementation and Improvement in Insomnia Symptoms Among Malaysian Women With Vitamin D Deficiency: #Protocol for a #RCT #ClinicalTrial

external.description: Background: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder associated with adverse physical, psychological, and functional outcomes. Emerging evidence suggests that vitamin D deficiency may contribute to sleep disturbances. Women are more likely to have lower serum vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D]) levels than men, and they also report a higher prevalence of insomnia. Although several studies have proposed that vitamin D supplementation may improve insomnia symptoms, findings remain inconsistent, and evidence from Southeast Asian populations is limited. Objective: This #Study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of weekly vitamin D₃ supplementation in improving insomnia symptoms, sleep quality, sleep efficiency, and functional outcomes among Malaysian women with vitamin D deficiency. Methods: This #Study is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomized placebo-controlled trial conducted among women aged 19‐50 years with serum 25(OH)D levels
external.title: Vitamin D Supplementation and Improvement in Insomnia Symptoms Among Malaysian Women With Vitamin D Deficiency: #Protocol for a #RCT #ClinicalTrial

record.text: JMIR Res Protocols: Clinical, Economic, and System-Level Outcomes of Bariatric Surgery in Adults: #Protocol for a Systematic Review

external.description: Background: Obesity affects approximately 880 million adults worldwide and carries substantial health, economic, and social consequences. Although bariatric surgery achieves sustained weight loss and metabolic improvement, existing systematic reviews largely predate 2020 and rarely integrate clinical, economic, and system-level perspectives within a single synthesis. Objective: This #Study aims to identify, critically appraise, and synthesize evidence published between 2020 and 2025 on the clinical effectiveness and economic impact of bariatric surgery in adults with obesity. A secondary, exploratory objective is to address system-level resource utilization, specifically length of stay, preoperative pathway duration, and outpatient care burden. Methods: This #Protocol follows the PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis #Protocols) 2015 guidance and is registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO: CRD420261351022). Eligible studies will enroll adults aged 18 years or older with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m) undergoing any primary bariatric procedure, including Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB), sleeve gastrectomy (SG), one-anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB), adjustable gastric banding (LAGB), and biliopancreatic diversion with or without duodenal switch (BPD±DS); revisional procedures are excluded as the index intervention. Eligible designs include #RCT #ClinicalTrials, cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, and economic evaluation studies published in English. MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science will be searched using predefined, database-tailored strategies; records will be managed in Zotero (Corporation for #Digital Scholarship). A single primary reviewer will perform screening, extraction, and risk-of-bias (RoB) assessment, with at least 20% independently duplicated by a second reviewer, weighted toward full-text and included studies. RoB will be assessed with RoB 2 and ROBINS-I (Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions); economic evaluations will be appraised for completeness of reporting with the CHEERS (Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards) 2022 statement and for methodological quality with the CHEC (Consensus on Health Economic Criteria) checklist. The primary synthesis will be narrative; meta-analysis will be considered only where prespecified comparability criteria are met. Certainty of evidence will be rated using GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation). Results: This #Protocol describes a review that is currently in progress. Registration with PROSPERO was completed on April 15, 2026, and database searches were run on August 1, 2026, identifying 9400 records. Title-and-abstract screening is scheduled to begin on August 15, 2026. Data extraction and synthesis are expected to be completed by the end of 2026, with publication of the completed review anticipated in the first half of 2027. Conclusions: This #Protocol provides a transparent and reproducible methodology for an integrated, contemporary synthesis of the clinical, economic, and system-level outcomes of bariatric surgery in adults. The findings are intended to inform health policy, resource planning, and future #Research priorities. Trial Registration: PROSPERO CRD420261351022; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261351022 International Registered Report Identifier (IRRID): PRR1-10.2196/98976
